mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of quarters where GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points for four consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower (p > 0.10) during periods of sustained unemployment rate increases above 0.3pp.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below the previous year's minimum for three consecutive months indicates a broad-based supply shock, which raises input costs and reduces profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < min(INDPRO last 12 months) for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual monetary and inflationary shock that increases real interest rates and erodes purchasing power, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and retail sales (proxied by RSAFS) above their 6-month averages signals strengthening household demand, which boosts corporate earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) when both PAYEMS and RSAFS exceed their 6-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 3.5% for six consecutive months signals an overheating labor market, which increases wage pressures and inflation expectations, ultimately resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to anticipated monetary tightening.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during periods of sustained sub-3.5% unemployment rates.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals a recovery in residential construction activity, which boosts demand for materials and labor and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) during periods when HOUST exceeds its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months.
